title: Slotted Capacity Micropanel: RBAC-aware controls for dedicated clusters
creator: Marina Chen
description: Deliver a compact, context-sensitive micropanel in the Redwood Console that surfaces per-slot health and operator controls for Dedicated GPU clusters. The micropanel (aka 'Slotted Capacity Micropanel') will be available from pool and cluster cards and from callouts in the fleet overview. Key capabilities: 1) read-only health summary (slot utilization, thermals, queued requests, top-k model variants), 2) safe autoscale quick actions (scale by +/-, set burst budget), 3) RBAC-aware escalation actions (drain slot, pin to reserve pool, trigger fallback model routing), and 4) lightweight cost preview and preflight checks to prevent accidental spend. Primary goals are reduce mean time to mitigation for on-call, enable safe operator interventions without full cluster navigation, and keep the surface usable for product teams (non-ops).
design_decisions: Micropanel is a contextual overlay anchored to pool/slot rows rather than a global modal to reduce clicks and keep workflows in context.
Show aggregate health signals (three-tier: OK/Degraded/Critical) instead of raw metric streams to avoid alert fatigue for PMs and product engineers.
Autoscale quick actions are limited to conservative presets with explicit cost previews to avoid accidental large commits.
RBAC: only users with 'pool-operator' role see escalation actions; engineers with 'viewer' role see read-only metrics and cost preview.
We decided to surface a single prominent fallback action (route-to-compatible-variant) rather than multiple fallback options in this iteration to keep complexity low.
Telemetry events will be emitted for every operator action for auditability and post-incident analysis; tradeoff is added ingestion cost which we'll cap via sampling on low-severity actions.
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff workshop with PM, Eng (runtime + infra), and Security. Captured UX constraints and must-have RBAC requirements.
2026-02-18: First wireframes completed. Focus on three-card layout: health summary, quick actions, cost preview. Shared Figma link.
2026-02-24: Engineering feasibility review: runtime team confirmed metrics available via new telemetry endpoint; agreed on optimistic 2-week integration for read-only data.
2026-03-01: High-fidelity prototype built; accessibility pass applied (contrast and keyboard focus). Prepared interactive flows for usability testing.
2026-03-04: Internal ops usability session with on-call rotation. Feedback captured and incorporated (added explicit 'safety hold' for burst toggles).
2026-03-05: Design docs updated, pushing ticket to In Review for PM and Security sign-off.
review_feedback: PM (Ayesha Khan): Prefer the cost preview to show both immediate delta and 24h projection. Suggest adding a lightweight 'why this matters' tooltip for product teams.
Runtime Eng (Diego Alvarez): Need clarity on the semantics of 'drain slot' and whether it triggers model cache eviction. Recommend adding a confirm modal and an API contract placeholder.
Security (Priya Nair): RBAC mapping OK; require security review for audit retention and KMS key use in any automated remediation actions. Marked security_review_required=true.
Design Peer (Lara Nguyen): Microcopy nit: replace 'burst budget' with 'burst allowance' to reduce confusion — accepted.
Ops reviewer (Marcus Lee): Add an explicit rollback knob when scaling down to avoid underprovisioning production traffic — added to follow-ups.

acceptance_criteria: Micropanel UI is reachable from pool and cluster rows in staging.
Read-only health summary displays aggregated signals and matches telemetry contract.
Autoscale quick actions perform dry-run cost preview and require explicit confirm for budget > $X/day.
Escalation actions are gated by RBAC and emit audit telemetry events.
Usability test (5 ops users) median task time to mitigation < 3 minutes.
Design tokens implemented and visual spec matches Figma within 2px tolerance for core elements.
